citations.narrative:
Penny's six puppies born 2-July-2026 and Marley's three puppies born 1-July-2026 and one additional foster puppy with
Marley's litter are not individually identified with an official identification number on the cage cards. The facility uses cage
cards as the litter's identification and inventory and the puppies are usually identified (microchip placed under the skin)
within one week of birth. Proper dog identification is required for APHIS officials to trace the movements of animals.
Ensure that each puppy under 16 weeks of age is properly identified in a timely manner.
To be corrected by: 30-July-2026

The facility is not creating medical records for female dogs having complications with whelping. The licensee is contacting
the attending veterinarian in a timely manner and following their guidance but failed to write any medical records detailing
when the issue was identified, plan for treatment and care and treatments performed. Three female dogs have had severe
complications with whelping since April 2026 and the licensee can verbally state most of the veterinarian guidance and
treatment plans but does not have anything recorded. Records of treatment for problems or diseases must be kept so that
APHIS officials can ensure that appropriate care is obtained for animals who are diseased, ill, or injured. The licensee
must keep and maintain records of any treatments given to animals in their care. Records should include the date and
description of the problem, examination findings, test results, a plan for treatment and care, and treatment procedures
performed.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
Additional Inspectors:
Jennifer Walker, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
